headline: Record King Tides and big surf keep moderate to major coastal flooding going into Friday (locally extreme at Thanksgiving morning's high tide) during a warm, dry stretch, before a strong Pacific storm next Tuesday and Wednesday brings a 75 to 85 percent chance of an inch or more of rain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving is sunny, warm and breezy as high pressure builds overhead. Dry east to northeast winds blowing out from the interior gust to around 35 mph along and below the coastal mountain slopes and through the passes, easing around noon. Highs jump 8 to 12 degrees from Wednesday in the valleys and inland coastal areas, running 12 to 18 degrees above average at the coast and in the western valleys, with the warmest spots inland from the coast into the western valleys reaching the lower to mid 80s. A band of high clouds moves in Thursday night into early Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday stays warm and dry, with the mountains and high desert warming about another 5 degrees. On Saturday the high pressure starts to weaken and the sea breeze returns, cooling the coast through the coastal mountain slopes by 4 to 8 degrees. Saturday highs are mostly mid 70s to around 80 at the coast and in the valleys, lower to mid 80s in the lower deserts, and mid 50s to mid 70s in the mountains.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cooling continues Sunday through Wednesday, and rain chances stay below 10 percent through Sunday. Sunday night and Monday bring about a 50 percent chance of showers from the coast to the mountains, though only a 15 to 25 percent chance of a quarter inch or more. A strong Pacific storm then moves into California Tuesday and Wednesday, with a 75 to 85 percent chance of 1 inch or more of rain from the coast to the mountains between Tuesday morning and Wednesday night; the chance of 3 inches or more ranges from under 10 percent near the coast to 35 to 45 percent in the San Bernardino County mountains. On the latest track and timing, the worst comes late Tuesday and Tuesday night, including strong winds and a chance of thunderstorms reaching coastal areas, and by Wednesday highs are only in the low 60s in the far inland valleys to upper 60s at the coast, 4 to 8 degrees below average in the mountains and inland valleys.

coast: Water levels set all-time records Wednesday morning: 8.65 feet at the San Diego Broadway Pier and 8.11 feet at La Jolla, both topping the records set October 27 of this year. King Tides continue Thursday, reaching about 8 feet Thursday morning, with tides running 1.1 to 1.2 feet above normal predictions. A long-period west swell (7 to 9 feet every 16 to 18 seconds) produces 6 to 8 foot breakers Thursday, with 10 to 12 foot sets on exposed west-facing beaches, easing to 3 to 7 feet Friday; a High Surf Advisory covers San Diego County beaches until 4 AM Friday. The record tides plus high surf bring moderate to major coastal flooding, locally extreme during Thursday morning's high tide, under a Coastal Flood Warning for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 1 PM Friday. Offshore, seas of 8 to 11 feet in the outer waters south of San Clemente Island and northwest gusts near 20 knots in the far outer waters bring a Small Craft Advisory (San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, 10 to 60 miles out, including San Clemente Island) until 10 AM Thursday, with seas dropping below 8 feet by evening. Next Tuesday night's storm could bring strong winds and thunderstorms over the coastal waters.
watch_for: Thanksgiving morning's high tide, when locally extreme coastal flooding is expected along with 6–8 foot surf
Timing and rain totals for next Tuesday–Wednesday's strong storm, with the worst currently expected late Tuesday and Tuesday night
Possible strong winds and thunderstorms reaching the coast with that storm
confidence: The warm, dry stretch through Saturday looks settled, and an inch or more of rain next Tuesday–Wednesday is likely (75 to 85 percent), but the timing of the heaviest weather depends on the storm's track in the latest computer models.
